passages.text: Where has your beloved gone, O most beautiful among women? Which way has he turned? We will seek him with you.
passages.sermon:
The daughters of Jerusalem speak to the woman.
They call her the most beautiful among women.
They ask her a question.
They say, "Where has your beloved gone?"
They ask, "Which way has your beloved turned?"
They say, "We will seek him with you."
passages.original: אָ֚נָה הָלַ֣ךְ דּוֹדֵ֔ךְ הַיָּפָ֖ה בַּנָּשִׁ֑ים אָ֚נָה פָּנָ֣ה דוֹדֵ֔ךְ וּנְבַקְשֶׁ֖נּוּ עִמָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to pasture his flock in the gardens and to gather lilies.
passages.sermon:
My beloved is a man who cares for his garden.
He went down to his own garden.
He went to the beds of spices.
He pastures his flock in the gardens.
He gathers lilies there.
passages.original: דּוֹדִי֙ יָרַ֣ד לְגַנּ֔וֹ לַעֲרוּג֖וֹת הַבֹּ֑שֶׂם לִרְעוֹת֙ בַּגַּנִּ֔ים וְלִלְקֹ֖ט שֽׁוֹשַׁנִּֽים׃

passages.text: I belong to my beloved and he belongs to me; he pastures his flock among the lilies.
passages.sermon:
The woman speaks about her beloved.
She says, "I belong to my beloved."
She also says, "My beloved belongs to me."
Her beloved is a shepherd.
He pastures his flock among the lilies.
passages.original: אֲנִ֤י לְדוֹדִי֙ וְדוֹדִ֣י לִ֔י הָרֹעֶ֖ה בַּשׁוֹשַׁנִּֽים׃ס

passages.text: You are as beautiful, my darling, as Tirzah, as lovely as Jerusalem, as majestic as troops with banners.
passages.sermon:
My darling, you are beautiful.
You are as beautiful as Tirzah.
You are as lovely as Jerusalem.
You are as majestic as armies with banners.
passages.original: יָפָ֨ה אַ֤תְּ רַעְיָתִי֙ כְּתִרְצָ֔ה נָאוָ֖ה כִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם אֲיֻמָּ֖ה כַּנִּדְגָּלֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Turn your eyes away from me, for they have overcome me. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down from Gilead.
passages.sermon:
The speaker addresses his beloved.
He asks her to turn her eyes away from him.
Her eyes have overcome him.
Her hair is beautiful.
Her hair is like a flock of goats.
The goats stream down from Gilead.
passages.original: הָסֵ֤בִּי עֵינַ֙יִךְ֙ מִנֶּגְדִּ֔י שֶׁ֥הֵ֖ם הִרְהִיבֻ֑נִי שַׂעְרֵךְ֙ כְּעֵ֣דֶר הָֽעִזִּ֔ים שֶׁגָּלְשׁ֖וּ מִן־ הַגִּלְעָֽד׃

passages.text: Your teeth are like a flock of sheep coming up from the washing; each has its twin, and not one of them is lost.
passages.sermon:
The speaker addresses his beloved woman.
He describes her teeth.
Her teeth are like a flock of sheep.
The sheep come up from the washing.
Each tooth has a matching pair.
None of her teeth are missing.
passages.original: שִׁנַּ֙יִךְ֙ כְּעֵ֣דֶר הָֽרְחֵלִ֔ים שֶׁעָל֖וּ מִן־ הָרַחְצָ֑ה שֶׁכֻּלָּם֙ מַתְאִימ֔וֹת וְשַׁכֻּלָ֖ה אֵ֥ין בָּהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Your brow behind your veil is like a slice of pomegranate.
passages.sermon:
The speaker addresses a woman he loves.
He describes her appearance.
He says, "Your brow is beautiful."
He sees her brow behind her veil.
He says her brow is like a slice of pomegranate.
Her brow is lovely and radiant.

passages.text: There are sixty queens and eighty concubines, and maidens without number, but my dove, my perfect one, is unique, the favorite of the mother who bore her. The maidens see her and call her blessed; the queens and concubines sing her praises.
passages.sermon:
There are sixty queens.
There are eighty concubines.
There are many maidens.
No one can count the maidens.
My dove is different from all of them.
My dove is perfect.
My dove is unique.
She is the only one of her mother.
She is the favorite of the woman who gave birth to her.
The maidens see her.
The maidens call her blessed.
The queens praise her.
The concubines praise her.
passages.original: שִׁשִּׁ֥ים הֵ֙מָּה֙ מְּלָכ֔וֹת וּשְׁמֹנִ֖ים פִּֽילַגְשִׁ֑ים וַעֲלָמ֖וֹת אֵ֥ין מִסְפָּֽר׃ אַחַ֥ת הִיא֙ יוֹנָתִ֣י תַמָּתִ֔י אַחַ֥ת הִיא֙ לְאִמָּ֔הּ בָּרָ֥ה הִ֖יא לְיֽוֹלַדְתָּ֑הּ רָא֤וּהָ בָנוֹת֙ וַֽיְאַשְּׁר֔וּהָ מְלָכ֥וֹת וּפִֽילַגְשִׁ֖ים וַֽיְהַלְלֽוּהָ׃ס

passages.text: Who is this who shines like the dawn, as fair as the moon, as bright as the sun, as majestic as the stars in procession?
passages.sermon:
A woman appears.
She shines like the dawn.
She is as beautiful as the moon.
She is as bright as the sun.
She is as majestic as the stars in procession.
passages.original: מִי־ זֹ֥את הַנִּשְׁקָפָ֖ה כְּמוֹ־ שָׁ֑חַר יָפָ֣ה כַלְּבָנָ֗ה בָּרָה֙ כַּֽחַמָּ֔ה אֲיֻמָּ֖ה כַּנִּדְגָּלֽוֹת׃ס

passages.text: I went down to the walnut grove to see the blossoms of the valley, to see if the vines were budding or the pomegranates were in bloom.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a beloved woman.
She went down to a walnut grove.
She wanted to see the valley.
She looked for blossoms there.
She wanted to see if the vines were budding.
She also wanted to see if the pomegranates were in bloom.
passages.original: אֶל־ גִּנַּ֤ת אֱגוֹז֙ יָרַ֔דְתִּי לִרְא֖וֹת בְּאִבֵּ֣י הַנָּ֑חַל לִרְאוֹת֙ הֲפָֽרְחָ֣ה הַגֶּ֔פֶן הֵנֵ֖צוּ הָרִמֹּנִֽים׃

passages.text: Before I realized it, my desire had set me among the royal chariots of my people.
passages.sermon:
A woman speaks in this passage.
She describes her experience.
She did not know what was happening.
Her soul moved her.
She found herself among the royal chariots.
These chariots belonged to her noble people.
passages.original: לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי נַפְשִׁ֣י שָׂמַ֔תְנִי מַרְכְּב֖וֹת עַמִּי־ נָדִֽיב׃

passages.text: Come back, come back, O Shulammite! Come back, come back, that we may gaze upon you. Why do you look at the Shulammite, as on the dance of Mahanaim ?
passages.sermon:
The Shulammite is a woman.
People call to her.
They say, "Come back, come back, O Shulammite."
They repeat, "Come back, come back."
They want to look at her.
They say, "Let us gaze upon you."
They ask a question.
They say, "Why do you look at the Shulammite?"
They compare her to something.
They say, "You look at her as at the dance of Mahanaim."
passages.original: שׁ֤וּבִי שׁ֙וּבִי֙ הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית שׁ֥וּבִי שׁ֖וּבִי וְנֶחֱזֶה־ בָּ֑ךְ מַֽה־ תֶּחֱזוּ֙ בַּשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית כִּמְחֹלַ֖ת הַֽמַּחֲנָֽיִם׃
